messages:
elena: Heads up — after the kernel swap to fp8-kernel-v3 + the new batching heuristic rollout, we’ve got a reproducible regression where structured JSON outputs are getting truncated/fields dropped. Canary and a small slice of prod show the same. Latency improved ~10% but eval deltas are bad.

elena: Quick repro example (canary request id: r-0a9f): expected "items" array but response ends with '...\n  "summary": "..."\n}' (missing items). Also some hallucinated object keys added in other cases.

elena: Perf/eval numbers from the A/B run (1000 samples):
```
A (int8-default): p95=180ms, tokens/s=420, QA-F1=86.2, structured-failure-rate=0.8%\nB (fp8-kernel-v3 + new-batcher): p95=162ms, tokens/s=458, QA-F1=81.8, structured-failure-rate=5.6%\nEval delta QA-F1: -4.4 absolute
```

elena: Profiler snippets show kernel choice flip at layer 12 and a KV cache hit pattern shift:
```
[profiler] chose kernel fp8_v3_sharded for layers 12-24
[kv] cache_index_offset: baseline=0x0, fp8-rollout=0x8 (per-batch)
[kv] cache_hits: A=98.6%, B=93.2%
```

elena: Config we changed: batching heuristics now pack variable-length requests into 256-token windows before dispatch. That interacts with the fp8 kernel's block alignment.

sanjay: Is the cache_index_offset change coming from the kernel's internal packing or from our batcher inserting padding differently?

elena: Quick root cause hypothesis: fp8 kernels use a different per-sequence padding alignment, which shifted KV indices when we applied the new pack-window heuristic. That causes some KV lookups to return stale/empty vectors for certain sequences -> garbled structured outputs.

tomas: Can you dump raw KV indices for a failing request? I want to see whether the per-step index equals expectation. Also check whether the kernel introduced a cast/trunc path that drops the high-bit for some offsets.

elena: Attached minimal trace for r-0a9f. Key lines: "kv_idx_seq=[0,1,2,3,8,9,...]" where we expected contiguous increments. Looks like a jump/skew at the batch boundary.

carmen: Recommendation: rollback the batcher change on canary immediately and keep fp8 kernel enabled on a small isolated pool until we validate. We should also run per-layer calibration sweep — maybe quant calibration produced a layer-specific alignment assumption.

elena: Agreed. Short plan:
1) Rollback batcher heuristic on canary (in flight).
2) Run per-layer KV-index trace on fp8-v3 across a few batch shapes (short/med/long).
3) Run our structured-output eval set (10k samples) with logging enabled.
4) If repro is confirmed, add a cache-warm policy at batch boundary as guard.

perf-bot: Automated snapshot for rollout window 2141234000-2141234600: tokens_total=2.4M, mean_latency_change=-9.8%, error_rate_change=+3.9% (structured failures). See /ops/perf/214123 for full histograms.

sanjay: Thanks. I'll help with the KV-index traces (taking an hour to run across canary). Tomas, do you want me to coordinate the per-layer calibration sweep?

tomas: Yes please — start with layers 8-16 where profiler shows the kernel switch. Use the full-calib schedule (1000 calib samples) and capture quantization stats.

carmen: I'll open a quick incident ticket and notify product about the eval delta so they can pause dependent rollouts. @elena prioritize a revert if we see structured-failure-rate > 2% on canary.

elena: Reverting batcher now on canary. Will post results of KV traces in this thread. Thanks :thumbsup:

elena: Follow-up (last update): rollback reduced structured-failure-rate back to baseline on canary. KV traces show the index skew disappears when pack-window is disabled. Next actions: add alignment fix in batcher to respect kernel block size + add a regression test to eval harness for structured JSON outputs.

elena: Pushed PR draft: rwd/runtime#4821 — batcher respect fp8 block-align. Requesting reviews from @tomas and @sanjay.
